clues: Either Kenji or Priya went home with the trophy.
One of Vera and whoever took home the medal won the sailboard race, and the other won the rowing race.
Kenji and the winner of the rowing race took home the ribbon and the pie, one each.
Of Kenji and the swim race winner, one got the ribbon and the other got the trophy.
hints: Look at the trophy. Clue 1 gives it two possible owners. Can another clue rule one of them out?
Clue 3 says Kenji took home either the ribbon or the pie. Read that beside clue 1.
So Kenji did not win the trophy, and by clue 1 Priya did. Then clues 2 and 3 leave the medal only for Della.

solution.key_idea: Clue 3 keeps Kenji from the trophy, so clue 1 hands it to Priya.
steps: By clue 3, Kenji took home the ribbon or the pie, so by clue 1 Priya won the trophy.
Clue 2 keeps Vera from the medal and clue 3 keeps Kenji from it, so the medal went to Della.
Clue 2 gives Della the sailboard or rowing race. Clue 3 gives the rowing winner the ribbon or pie, so Della won the sailboard race.
Clue 2 gives Vera the rowing race. Clue 4 keeps Kenji from the swim race, so Kenji won the kayak race and Priya the swim.
By clue 3, Kenji took the ribbon or pie, and clue 4 rules out the pie, so Kenji took the ribbon and Vera the pie.
solution.epilogue: The Gazette went to press on time, captions and all: Priya's swim trophy, Kenji's kayak ribbon, Della's sailboard medal, and Vera's rowing-race pie, which she shared with the newsroom.

tip: When a clue gives someone just two choices, look for another clue that takes one away.
